name: butter

attributes.attribute: linked in folklore to fairies and witchcraft
the leftover liquid, consumed as a nourishing drink
could fail to come from the liquid milk during churning

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Butter held a folkloric link to fairies and to witchcraft. Rural life in Ireland and Scotland turned on cattle. The herd gave milk, butter, cheese and meat. Churning butter from cow's milk was a core part of women's work in these lands. The maker beat the milk until the butterfat set into a yellow mass. The leftover buttermilk served as a nourishing drink. The butter itself was shaped and stored for later use. At any stage the work could go wrong and spoil the butter into a half-set, half-liquid mess. The usual complaint was that the butter would not come from the liquid milk. No matter how hard the woman churned, the butter stayed thin.

okr.objective: Present butter as a folkloric object tied to fairies and to the churning work of women.
key_results: Butter was connected in folklore to fairies and witchcraft.
Churning milk to set the butterfat was core women's work in Ireland and Scotland.
The leftover buttermilk was drunk as a nourishing drink.
The butter could spoil, leaving a half-set, half-liquid mess.
